prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Columbus Ohio for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car-accident case — the right attorney depends on the specifics of your crash, injuries, and goals. I can help you find a strong fit, but here’s a practical approach you can use immediately.

Quick actions (if you haven’t already)
- Get medical care and follow doctors’ orders (medical records are essential to a claim).
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles, injuries, scene, traffic signs; witness names/contacts.
- Don’t give recorded statements to the other side or sign releases from insurers without talking to an attorney.
- Note date/time/location and police report number. File a claim quickly.

How to find the best lawyer for your case in Columbus
1. Look for a specialist
   - Choose attorneys who focus on car-accident/personal-injury litigation (not general practice).
   - Check they handle cases like yours (whiplash, catastrophic injury, wrongful death).

2. Check credentials and track record
   - Look for trial experience and recent settlements/verdicts in similar cases.
   - Peer ratings (AV Preeminent from Martindale-Hubbell), Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, and local bar awards can help but read the underlying results.
   - Read multiple client reviews (Google, Avvo, Yelp) for consistency.

3. Practical fit
   - Contingency fee agreement (typical for PI: attorney is paid only if you recover).
   - Clear communication and responsiveness.
   - Resources to take a case through trial if needed (some small firms settle quickly; larger firms may be able to litigate).

4. Local resources to search
   - Columbus Bar Association lawyer referral
   - Ohio State Bar Association lawyer referral
   - Super Lawyers (Ohio/Columbus)
   - Martindale-Hubbell and Avvo
   - Google Maps local search + reviews

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- Do you handle car-accident/personal-injury cases full time?
- How many cases like mine have you handled? Any recent results?
- Will you handle my case personally or will associates/paralegals work on it?
- Do you accept cases on contingency? What is your fee percentage and are there other costs?
- What should I expect for timeline and communication?
- Do you have trial experience? Have you taken similar cases to verdict?

Important legal note
- Ohio’s statute of limitations for most personal-injury claims is two years from the injury date (Ohio Rev. Code § 2305.10). Don’t delay contacting an attorney.

If you want, tell me:
- Brief facts (injuries, severity, fault level, insurance issues), and whether you prefer a large firm or a solo practitioner — I can then suggest how to narrow to top candidates and draft a short message to send to potential lawyers or a list of specific Columbus firms you can start with.
